items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: that’s why I always compare it to English composition even. You know you have to have an introduction, you introduce your theme, your thesis, you develop it, you recapitulate, you do a summarization and then you lock up and bow as Kenny Dorham used to say.

ctx.x: Or the demented scale. And they have to understand that you’re composing music. And you have to relate to your audience. Nobody wants to come and hear you practice. I don’t want to come and hear you sit up and play exercises. I mean do that in your house or in your practice room or something like that. You have to learn how to compose music. That’s the beauty of jazz. You’re called upon to be an instantaneous composer. You have to learn how to build your solos. I hear these kids, they’re just playing ad…
That’s so interesting because also, those guys had to operate in a time when the length on a record was very limited.
